outcomeNote: A mishna lemma with a tannaitic dissent; no argument is conducted here.

segments.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל הַפַּת, פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת. עַל הַפַּרְפֶּרֶת, לֹא פָּטַר אֶת הַפַּת. בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אַף לֹא מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «One who recited a blessing over the bread exempted the appetizers,» as they are considered secondary to the bread. However, one who recited a blessing «over the appetizers did not exempt the bread. Beit Shammai say:» The blessing recited over the appetizers «did not exempt even a cooked dish» that he eats during the meal.

moves.cueHe: ברך על הפת, פטר את הפרפרת
moves.summary: Mishna: a blessing over bread exempts the appetizers; a blessing over the appetizers does not exempt the bread
moves.about: the gemara restates the mishna's lemma on blessings over bread, appetizers and cooked dishes

moves.summary: Beit Shammai dissent: the blessing does not exempt even a cooked dish
moves.about: whether the blessing (over appetizers, on Steinsaltz's reading) exempts even a cooked dish eaten in the meal — Beit Shammai say it does not
